reason: Arm (1) identity check is sound but tautological (Tr(b/x^2)=Tr(beta/x)); it is a unit test, not a discriminator. Arm (2) is under-powered at l=4: null 2^-15=3.05e-5 x 2e5 samples = ~6 expected hits, so a 1.5x excess (9 vs 6, sd~2.5) can never reach p<1e-3; only l=3 (~1560 hits, sd~39) discriminates. Arm (4) falsifier 'sigma_V=0 at dim>=3' is not a discriminator: sigma_V = c1/c0 of the subspace polynomial, so sigma_V=0 occurs by chance with prob 2^-n per subspace (~100 hits in 2e5 at n=11); it is a necessary condition only (1 bit), and the derivation is wrong when Tr(a)=1 (sum over V\0 of an affine function with constant c is c, not 0, so condition is Tr(beta sigma_V)=Tr(a)). Arm (3) 'beta/x-closed all-lift family' is ill-defined: x->beta/x is not linear so beta/V is not a subspace; the correct statement is beta/V\0 is an all-lift non-subspace set (lift status is invariant), which is trivially true. The 'factor growing n=11->13' criterion uses two points and is already covered by the programme census (0.92x null at N=11, p=2e-5), so the experiment mostly re-measures a known number. Toy-to-n=131 link: l=3,4 at n=11,13 says nothing about l ~ n/2 needed for a factor base; the lever only matters if all-lift subspaces of growing dimension exist, so the right toy quantity is max all-lift dimension l*(n) against a matched random-set null across primes n, not a fraction at fixed l. The literature step (sum-freedom of inverse function) concerns the vectorial map; here only one Boolean component Tr(beta/x) must be affine, which is weaker, so 'closes lever 7 structurally' does not follow from the census either way (census = evidence, not closure). Metric is a structural count (subspace counts, dimension), not wall time: OK. Runtime: fine in python3/numpy (<20 CPU-min) once redesigned. Classification relabelling stands: even a positive result is a constant factor by the twist closure (nongenericity argument = none).
fix: Keep the n in {11,13}, K_0 + 8 random b, but redesign: (A) Replace uniform sampling with exact counts of all-lift subspaces by DFS over Z={x!=0: Tr(x)+Tr(beta/x)=Tr(a)} (|Z|~2^{n-1}): enumerate l=2 exactly (n=11 and 13), then extend to l=3,4 with canonical-basis (echelon) ordering and bitset/numpy membership table; if n=13 l=4 too heavy, use sequential importance sampling (pick v1 in Z, v2 in Z with v1+v2 in Z, ... with weights = product of candidate counts) giving unbiased estimator with ~1e5 chains and relative error reported. (B) Null arms: (i) exact expectation for a random set of the same size |Z| (count_subspaces(n,l) * prod over 2^l-1 points of hypergeometric ratio), (ii) Monte-Carlo control with Z replaced by random subsets of equal density and by Z' = {x: Tr(x)+Tr(g(x))=c} for a random permutation g with same pair-orbit structure (preserve x<->beta/x pairing: shuffle at the orbit level, since lift status is constant on {x,beta/x}), so the null keeps the involution correlation; (iii) positive control: plant a known affine-on-V case (b chosen so Tr(beta/x) is constant on a chosen V is infeasible, so instead plant V in a random Z) to show the estimator recovers a planted subspace. Report ratio observed/null with Poisson CI, per curve, per (n,l). (C) Add the scaling quantity: maximal all-lift dimension l*(n) via greedy+DFS, for primes n=7,11,13,17,19 (n=17,19 via importance sampling / greedy only) vs the same quantity for the orbit-shuffled null; prediction_if_true: l*(n) tracks null (about log2 of n-ish growth, within +-1), ratio->1 with n; prediction_if_false: l*(n) exceeds null by >=2 dims at n>=13 or ratio rises monotonically over n=11,13,17,19 with CI excluding 1. (D) Drop 'sigma_V=0' as a falsifier; replace with test that Tr(beta sigma_V)=Tr(a) holds for 100% of all-lift V with l>=2 (exact necessary-condition check, 100% required, else bug) and that the fraction of subspaces with sigma_V=0 is 2^-n (null). (E) Replace 'beta/x-closed family' with: count all-lift V such that beta/V\0 is contained in another all-lift subspace's support (i.e. beta/V is a subspace) -- expected near 0 for l>=2; report any hit explicitly. (F) State in verdict text that a null-matching census yields 'no evidence of structure at toy n', not a closure; do not write 'closes lever 7' without a proof of an l*(n) upper bound.
